outlook.statement: Pending identification of new growth opportunities surplus funds arising from such divestments have been deployed in treasury and other investment avenues in accordance with applicable provisions of the Companies Act 2013. The primary objectives of such deployment are preservation of funds, maintenance of adequate liquidity and generation of reasonable risk-adjusted returns.

The Company enters the next phase of its journey with a debt-light balance sheet, substantial liquidity and the flexibility to pursue new growth and attractive opportunities. The strong financial position provides the Company with the ability to evaluate opportunities without immediate capital constraints and to respond swiftly to favourable market conditions.

India's economic outlook remains resilient and growth-driven as of mid-August 2025. Recorded GDP growth of 6.5% in FY 2024-25 (with 7.4% in Q4) outpaced earlier expectations. Forecasts for FY 2025-26 anticipate growth between 6.3% and 6.8%.
The Board of Directors of Company is evaluating potential business opportunities for future deployment of funds.

Subsequent to the year ended March 31, 2026, the Board of Directors of the Holding Company, at the meeting held on May 29, 2026, recommended dividend at the rate 10% (Rs. 0.20/- per equity share of par value of Rs. 2/- each) for the year ended March 31, 2026, subject to the approval of members in the ensuing Annual General Meeting. The total dividend outgo shall be Rs. 314.10 lakhs.

The Holding Company has deposited a sum of Rs. 250 Lakhs with the registrar of Supreme Court of India in term of order passed on 14th December 2023 by Hon'ble Supreme Court in respect of Special Leave Petition (SLP) filed by the Holding company against the order passed by Hon'ble High Court on October 23, 2023 for Writ Petition filed by tenants.

The Holding Company had received two orders dated April 10, 2024 and June 26, 2024 from office of the Commissioner of Customs, Goa and the Commissioner of Customs, Nhava Sheva, Maharashtra claiming a IGST duty demand of Rs. 1854.17 Lakhs (including penalty and fine of Rs. 1045.94 Lakhs) plus applicable interest, towards non payment of IGST at the time of import of material due to non fulfilment of pre-import condition under Advance Authorisation Scheme under section 28(4) of Customs Act 1962. The Holding Company had filed an appeal against the said Orders on July 18 2024 and July 10, 2024. The appeals are pending with Commissioner of Customs, Excise & Service Tax Appellate Tribunal.

The Group's pending litigations comprise of claim against the Group and proceedings pending with Statutory and Tax Authorities. The Group has reviewed all its pending litigations and proceedings and has made adequate provisions, whenever required and disclosed the contingent liabilities, whenever applicable, in its financial statements. The Group does not expect the outcome of these proceedings to have a material impact on its financial position.
